text:
morgan_cs: FYI forwarding ACME infra report — their python streaming generator is hanging intermittently after auth refreshes and a run of 429s. Logs + repro below, asked if this is a known bug.

morgan_cs: customer says downgrading the SDK fixed it (0.8.7 works, 0.9.1 hangs). adding logs. req_id=abc123 correlation_id=acme-42

morgan_cs: LOG SNIPPET:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11.234Z INFO client.py:stream opening SSE connection
2026-03-15T14:02:12.012Z WARN auth.py token refresh started
2026-03-15T14:02:12.110Z ERROR http 401 refresh failed -> retry
2026-03-15T14:02:12.112Z INFO http retry attempt=1 429
2026-03-15T14:02:12.113Z SSE CHUNK: "data: {\"delta\": \"Hel"
2026-03-15T14:02:12.114Z SSE CHUNK: "lo, worl"
2026-03-15T14:02:12.115Z SSE CHUNK: "d\", \"done\": false}\n\n"
2026-03-15T14:02:12.200Z INFO generator: waiting for next event (blocked)
```

morgan_cs: repro steps the customer provided:
1) pip install redwood==0.9.1
2) start a streaming chat with long-ish first token sequence (utf-8 multi-byte characters + emojis)
3) force token refresh (invalidate key) while stream active
4) observe generator no longer yields despite SSE data arriving in several small TCP frames

liam_eng: thanks. did they use the default retry policy? 0.9.x added aggressive immediate retries on 401->429 which can reorder read loop vs auth refresh.

morgan_cs: yes default. they didn't customize retry/backoff.

sara_ml: suspect: SSE parser assumes each event payload arrives as a single .read() chunk boundary. when auth refresh triggers a socket reset/mini-reconnect we can get byte-split JSON (mid-utf8) and our incremental parser falls back to waiting for \n

also race between reconnect and generator consumer cancellation can leave the generator awaiting buffer that never completes. seen this with AB-2456 earlier.

sara_ml: quick workaround for customer: set CLIENT_STREAM_KEEPALIVE env to 1 and relax retry policy (exponential backoff) or pin to 0.8.7. but we need a proper fix (stream parser resilient to partial utf-8 / boundary tokens + cancel-safe reconnect).

liam_eng: can you paste minimal client snippet they run?

morgan_cs: here's their minimal loop:
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
with client.stream_chat(model='gpt-lite') as gen:
    for event in gen:
        if event.type == 'delta':
            print(event.delta, end='')
        elif event.type == 'done':
            break
```

morgan_cs: they implemented SSE parsing using the default SDK generator (no custom parsing).

liam_eng: OK. repro plan: 1) run with network capture to confirm byte-split of UTF-8 / JSON, 2) reproduce locally by injecting a small sleep in server chunking, 3) try canary wheel with parser fallback enabled.

liam_eng: test wheel command (internal canary):
```
pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python@fix/sse-byte-split#egg=redwood
```

liam_eng: note: this branch adds incremental UTF-8 reassembly and moves auth refresh to a background thread so read loop isn't blocked by 401 handling.

morgan_cs: passed the wheel to customer, they installed and reported the hang no longer reproduces in the quick test. they still see occasional latency spikes because retry storm after 429s adds head-of-line delay.

sara_ml: for the retry storm, recommend config change in customer app: set REDWOOD_RETRY_POLICY=max_retries=3,backoff=exponential(0.5, factor=2). also add jitter. We'll add a server-side safeguard to avoid aggressive immediate retries on 401 that can interact poorly with streaming.

liam_eng: creating ENG-INC bug: ENG-RT-2456 streaming parser + auth-race. marking P1 for dedicated rollback if needed. attaching customer logs (req_id=abc123).

deploy-bot: scheduled patch deploy to canary at 2026-03-16T02:00:00Z (rollout 10%).

morgan_cs: customer confirmed canary fixed hang; will run prolonged soak. asked for timeline to GA patch.

liam_eng: target release for stable patch in 48 hours pending soak. will also prepare SDK patch release 0.9.2 with regression tests for byte-split SSE and auth-refresh interleaving.

morgan_cs: thank you — I'll keep customer updated. asking if we should bill this as SLA credit? customer requested credit for multi-hour outage window, forwarding to finance after we resolve.

sara_ml: ack — document root cause once fixed and send postmortem. include repro and recommended customer config (keepalive + reduced immediate retry).

morgan_cs: will follow up once soak completes. closing loop later. :thumbsup:
